proposed_sites.reason: mcp.server.fastmcp module path is removed in v2 and moves to mcp.server.mcpserver; additionally FastMCP is renamed to MCPServer, so both the import path and the imported identifier must change to `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer`.
Constructs the server using the old class name FastMCP; per the migration spec this class is renamed to MCPServer, so this call site must become MCPServer(name="secops-mcp", ...).

considered_and_rejected.snippet: cmd = ["httpx", "-json", "-l", "-"]  # Use stdin for list input
considered_and_rejected.reason: This invokes the external ProjectDiscovery `httpx` CLI security tool via subprocess, not the Python httpx package and not the MCP SDK's internal HTTP transport dependency. Rule 6 explicitly says the SDK's httpx->httpx2 change is internal and irrelevant to unrelated application usage of the word/package 'httpx'.
Imports this repo's own tools/httpx.py module (a CLI wrapper), unrelated to the Python httpx package or MCP SDK transport.
Name coincidentally matches 'httpx' but is a wrapper function for the ProjectDiscovery httpx CLI tool, not related to the MCP SDK's transport dependency.

The @mcp.tool() decorator is explicitly confirmed unchanged in the migration spec; same applies to all other @mcp.tool() decorator usages throughout main.py (lines 42, 52, 62, 72, 82, 92, 101, 110, 119, 128, 136, 145, 155, 182, 207, 236, 255).
mcp.run() is not among the confirmed changes in the migration spec; only the FastMCP class name/import path and Context import path are affected, not the run() method's behavior or signature.

This is a transitive pinned dependency version (used internally by requests/mcp), not an application call site in code; and per rule 6 the SDK's internal httpx dependency change is not something application code needs to react to.
